description.para: This parameter forces winbindd 8 to use a specific Active Directory site for a domain, instead of relying on the normal CLDAP-based site auto-discovery.

Without this option, winbind determines the site it belongs to by sending a CLDAP ping to a Domain Controller and using the site name the Domain Controller returns, based on the AD Sites and Subnets configuration on the Domain Controller matching the client's source address. This works well as long as the client's outgoing address is correctly mapped to a site in Active Directory, but does not help when, for example, firewall rules restrict which Domain Controllers a client is actually allowed to reach and that set of Domain Controllers does not match what Active Directory's own subnet mapping would have picked.

This parameter consists of the prefix, followed by a colon and the DNS domain (realm) name the site should be forced for, and is set to the name of the Active Directory site to use for that domain. Each domain is configured independently, so a site can be forced for one domain while another is left on normal auto-discovery.

When set for a domain, winbind restricts its DNS SRV lookups and DC selection to the given site for that domain, and does not fall back to whichever site a contacted Domain Controller reports as the client's closest site. If no Domain Controller can be found for the forced site, winbind falls back to a site-less lookup, the same way it does when auto-discovery finds no Domain Controller for the discovered site.
The following example forces winbind to use the Site-HQ Active Directory site for the EARTH.ORG domain, while MILKWAY.ORG continues to use normal site auto-discovery:
Multiple domains can each be forced to their own site:
description.programlisting: winbind ad site : EARTH.ORG = Site-HQ winbind ad site : MILKWAY.ORG = Site-Core
description.para: The currently discovered or forced site for a domain can be checked with wbinfo --dsgetdcname=DOMAIN, which prints the Domain Controller's own site (dc_site_name) and the client's site (client_site_name):
